sentences.text: Today, we will talk about Kosovo.
Kosovo is a small, young, and friendly country in southeastern Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Kosovo?
Kosovo is in the Balkans, in southeastern Europe.
It borders Serbia, Albania, North Macedonia, and Montenegro.
It is a landlocked country, which means it has no sea.
What is the capital city of Kosovo?
The capital city is Pristina.
Pristina is the largest city in Kosovo.
It has universities, markets, cafes, and many young people.
Other cities include Prizren, an old and beautiful city, Peja near the mountains, Djakova and Mitrovica.
How many people live in Kosovo?
About one eight million people live in Kosovo.
Most people live in cities or towns.
The people are called Kosovars and many are ethnic Albanians.
What language do people speak in Kosovo?
The official languages are Albanian Serbian.
Some people also speak Bosnian, Turkish, and Romani.
English is popular, especially among young people.
What is the weather like in Kosovo?
Kosovo has a continental climate.
Hot summers, cold winters with snow.
Spring and autumn are mild and beautiful.
The seasons are clear and change every few months.
What does Kosovo look like?
Kosovo has mountains great for hiking and skiing, rivers, valleys, and forests, traditional villages, green fields, and small farms.
It is a country with clean air and lovely nature.
What animals live in Kosovo?
In nature, you can find foxes, wolves, and deer, eagles, owls, and other birds.
Sheep, goats, and cows on farms.
Dogs and cats in towns.
Some mountain areas are home to bears, but they are rare.
What do people eat in Kosovo?
Kosovo food is simple, tasty, and often homemade.
People eat bread, cheese, and yogurt.
Meat like lamb, beef, or chicken.
Beans, rice, and potatoes.
Peppers, cabbage, and tomatoes.
Popular dishes.
Flea -layered pastry baked over fire.
Tavekosi, lamb with yogurt sauce.
Pie with cheese or spinach.
Sarma, meat and rice in cabbage leaves.
Grilled meat like chabapa and sausages.
What do people drink in Kosovo?
People drink water and fruit juice.
Coffee, very popular, especially Turkish coffee.
Tea, often with lemon.
Adults may drink rakia, a fruit brandy.
Buttermilk or iron in summer.
Coffee is a big part of daily life.
People sit and talk for hours.
What is life like in Kosovo?
Life in Kosovo is warm, family -based, and social.
People enjoy visiting family and friends.
Going to cafes, helping neighbors.
Dancing at weddings.
Spending time in nature.
Many people live in big family homes and share meals together.
What are some holidays and traditions in Kosovo?
Independence Day, February 17th.
Flag Day, Albanian culture, November 28th.
Eid al -Fitr and Eid al -Adha for Muslims.
Christmas and Easter for Christians.
Weddings and folk festivals with music and dancing.
Traditional dance is called vale and is done in a circle.
Some fun facts about Kosovo.
Kosovo became independent in 2008.
The flag is blue and yellow with a map of the country and six stars.
It is one of the youngest countries in the world.
Over 50 % of the population is under 30 years old.
Music and hospitality are a big part of the culture.
Now you know many things about Kosovo.
You know where it is, what people speak, and what they eat.
You learned about the land, traditions, and daily life.
Great job!
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I'm Emily.
